extendedContent.title: Origins & Mythology
extendedContent.content: Dôn's origins are shrouded in the mists of early Celtic belief, but her connection to the Irish goddess Danu suggests a shared Proto-Celtic ancestry. In Welsh mythology, she is primarily known as the mother of a powerful lineage of gods and heroes. While explicit narratives focusing solely on Dôn are limited, she is implicitly present in the stories of her children. The most prominent source referencing Dôn is the Mabinogion, a collection of medieval Welsh tales. Her children's actions and stories reflect her influence as a matriarchal figure. Her name is synonymous with the house of Dôn, a powerful family within the Welsh pantheon.

extendedContent.title: Role & Significance
extendedContent.content: Dôn's significance lies in her role as the mother of a divine lineage. She embodies the concept of fertility and the cyclical nature of life and death. Her children's roles in various myths highlight the importance of family and ancestry in Welsh Celtic culture. As a mother goddess, Dôn's influence extends beyond her direct actions, shaping the destinies of her offspring and impacting the overall narrative of Welsh mythology. Her association with Annwn, the Welsh Otherworld, suggests a connection to the realm of the dead and the continuation of life beyond the physical world.

extendedContent.title: Symbolism & Interpretation
extendedContent.content: Dôn symbolizes motherhood, fertility, and the continuity of generations. She represents the source of life and the ancestral connection that binds individuals to their past. Her association with the Otherworld suggests a connection to the cyclical nature of existence and the transformative power of death and rebirth. The limited direct narratives about Dôn could be interpreted as a reflection of the subtle yet pervasive influence of the feminine divine in Celtic belief. She embodies the quiet strength and enduring power of motherhood, shaping the world through her descendants.

extendedContent.title: Legacy & Influence
extendedContent.content: Dôn's legacy continues to resonate in modern interpretations of Celtic mythology and spirituality. She is often invoked as a symbol of feminine power, ancestral connection, and the enduring strength of family. Her name appears in various neopagan and Wiccan traditions, where she is honored as a mother goddess and a source of inspiration. Although not as widely known as some other Celtic deities, Dôn remains a significant figure for those interested in exploring the rich tapestry of Welsh mythology and its enduring impact on contemporary culture. Her children, especially Gwydion and Arianrhod, are far more prominent in modern retellings of Celtic myths and legends.

description: Dôn is a prominent figure in Welsh mythology, revered as a mother goddess and considered the ancestor of many significant characters. Her name, meaning "lady" or "mistress," reflects her status as a powerful and influential figure. She is often compared to the Irish goddess Danu, suggesting a shared Celtic origin and a common role as a mother of gods. Dôn's children, known as the Children of Dôn, comprise a significant portion of the Welsh pantheon, including figures like Gwydion, Arianrhod, and Gilfaethwy. While specific myths directly involving Dôn are scarce, her role as a progenitor places her at the heart of many narratives within the Mabinogion. Her influence is felt through the actions and destinies of her offspring, shaping the course of events in the mythological landscape of Wales. She is considered a figure of fertility, abundance, and ancestral power.
shortDescription: Welsh mother goddess, equivalent to the Irish Danu, and mother to a pantheon of gods and heroes.
